thread:
kyle: kicking off config-only deploy to canary-2 — rate caps and batching tweaks. 30m dry-run then ramp. @anika @jiang please watch dashboards and call for rollback if anything looks off.

deploy-bot: job 7842 started on canary-2. Changes applied (config-only):
- rate_cap_rps: 12 -> 8
- batching_window_ms: 25 -> 40
- idle_timeout_ms: 1200 -> 800
- routing_policy: prefer-cost-over-latency

anika: quick q — confirming no model change? pinning v4.1.2?

kyle: correct, model pinned to v4.1.2. No weight changes.

jiang: observability checklist: p95 latency, error-rate, queue-depth, KV cache-miss rate. I’ll add transient alerts: error_rate > 3% or p95 > 450ms.

ops-sre: running synthetic ramp (2x expected QPS) against canary-2 now to exercise tails.

deploy-bot: dry-run metrics posted: https://kibana.internal/infra/dashboard/job/7842 — sample: p50 92ms, p95 410ms, errors 0.7%, queue-depth avg 1.2. No immediate regressions seen.

anika: looks reasonable but small p95 uplift vs baseline (baseline p95 ~380ms). Suspect batching_window -> 40ms effect.

kyle: expected a slight p95 increase; tradeoff is lower per-token cost. Plan: 30m dry-run, then 20% traffic for 10m if stable, then full roll. Rollback playbook ready.

jiang: prepared rollback commands and idempotent revert: `./scripts/release/rollback-config --job 7842 --target canary-2` and manual override to set `batching_window_ms=25` and `rate_cap_rps=12`.

ops-sre: monitoring continuum — will call if tail or KV misses spike.

deploy-bot: transitioning to 20% traffic for canary-2 (promote step).

ops-sre: alert — p95 spiked to 560ms at minute 41 of run, error rate climbed to 1.4%. Redis cache-miss rate up ~3x. Observed long-sequence sessions queued behind small ones (head-of-line).

anika: :warning: proposing immediate rollback. Voting: rollback? react with :thumbsup: to roll back.

kyle: :thumbsup: — rollback now.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated for job 7842. Reverting batching_window_ms->25 and rate_cap_rps->12. Rollback completed at ts 1777777320.

jiang: quick post-mortem note: root cause appears to be interaction between increased batching_window and routing_policy that favored cost paths, producing KV cache pressure for a subset of long-sequence traffic.

kyle: adding to release notes: config-only attempt on 2026-03-20 (job 7842) dry-run then rollback due to p95 and cache misses. Next plan: add targeted canary with long-seq heavy synthetic load, tune batching logic (maybe dynamic window by sequence length), and add KV-pressure synthetic test to preflight.

anika: also recommend adding a small automated safety: if cache-miss rate > 2x baseline for 5m during canary, auto-suspend config promotion.

jiang: noted, will add the safety check and the synthetic test to the rollout checklist.

ops-sre: closing watch. No further action needed now. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
